### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via bootstrapDeclaredPermissions (symbol, a top-level function), upsertPackagePermissionSet (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via bootstrapDeclaredPermissions (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 841ed38947850738cf6ac12388abbd7029a2a7b9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `055fe9e608e1035fd6cc7bdfe0feb79e0c0c4793` — the merge of head `953e2bc357f6520c62ea4013e5734cf70deb5ed0` into base `841ed38947850738cf6ac12388abbd7029a2a7b9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 055fe9e608e1035fd6cc7bdfe0feb79e0c0c4793 && git checkout 055fe9e608e1035fd6cc7bdfe0feb79e0c0c4793
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 841ed38947850738cf6ac12388abbd7029a2a7b9 953e2bc357f6520c62ea4013e5734cf70deb5ed0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 841ed38947850738cf6ac12388abbd7029a2a7b9 && git merge --no-ff 953e2bc357f6520c62ea4013e5734cf70deb5ed0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 841ed38947850738cf6ac12388abbd7029a2a7b9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 841ed38947850738cf6ac12388abbd7029a2a7b9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

`5754242454` 名下两页,逐页量过,⛔ 不是按包名一扫了事:

**① `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` —— 无事可做。** 它在 `:145` 与 `:219` 点名了本 diff 动过的两个符号,但两处都是**行为叙述**,⛔ 不是 `PermissionSeedOutcome` 字段的枚举:`:145-149` 说的是「幂等、升级时重播、从不覆写 env-authored 行、一个包从不写进外来记录」,`:219` 说的是 publish materializer 复用 boot seeder 的同一把 upsert。整页 577 行里 `PermissionSeedOutcome` / `skipped` / `unowned` / `counter` **一个都不出现**。⇒ 本 diff **没有证伪该页任何一句**;补一个 `skippedUnowned` 之后,它说的每一句仍然为真。

⭐ 这一条是**重新核实**,不是豁免:漂移检查自己的措辞就是「**may** need an implementation-accuracy re-verification」—— 它指的是「该重读一遍」,核实由人做,做完才有结论。本席做了,结论是不欠。

**② `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx` —— ⛔ release-owned,只读。** 按 AGENTS.md〈Documentation Guardrails〉,发版说明在发版时集中撰写,而「一个代码 PR 去改它」正是该护栏存在要拦的那种 PR。⇒ 本 PR ⛔ 不碰它。若它确有错,走立卡或专门的 docs-only PR,⛔ 不在这里顺手改。

⇒ **本轮不增加 docs 提交**,dev 已被告知同一判读,⛔ 不必重复推导,也 ⛔ 不得因这条机器人评论而动上面任何一页。

⚠️ 一条不宣称的边界:上表只核了漂移检查**点名的那两页**。该检查自己的〈What this run could not see〉段落列了三类它结构上看不见的漏检(路由桥只覆盖 215 行中的 60 行、按输入陈述规则的页与实现它的发射点不共享标识符、键名不等于键)。⇒ 本席 ⛔ 不宣称「本 diff 没有影响任何其它文档」—— 那句话这把尺子给不出,本席也没有另行量过。

### ① Derived judgments

`PermissionSeedOutcome` (`permission-set-projection.ts:223`), barrel-exported at `src/index.ts:125` and re-exported at `bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts:85`, gains a **required** `skippedUnowned: number`, incremented on the `!packageId` refusal branch. Public-surface change, correctly named.

**Required-vs-optional matches the tree's own discriminator, ⛔ not the author's preference.** On this interface the OPTIONAL members are the ones whose ABSENCE carries meaning (`collisions?` — 「absent, never `[]`, when the pass hit none」; `deleted?` — produced only by the retire door and explicitly not to be read as a count). The REQUIRED members are the refusal/outcome counts every door initialises so a reader can sum unconditionally. `skippedUnowned` is the latter, and it is the exact spelling of its sibling `CapabilitySeedOutcome.skippedUnowned`.

**Accounting: non-double-counting — verified branch by branch.** Every branch of `upsertPackagePermissionSet` increments exactly one counter and returns; the boot aggregator forwards each of the seven once (`:420-427`); the ADR-0086 P2 publish door passes no collector and returns the per-set outcome directly, so it sees the increment without aggregation. Both doors covered.

**The CONSERVATION pin catches a double count, ⛔ not only a zero** — `bootstrap-declared-permissions.test.ts:485-489` pins each counter's exact value AND `:493-495` pins the seven-counter sum against the input count; a compensating swap is caught by the lone-orphan and lone-foreign cases together. The reviewer verified the routing of all six inputs rather than trusting the test's own labels.

**The sweep was re-run independently and came back STRONGER than the PR claimed**: zero consumers of the type in **any** role — reader or constructor — across objectstack, the pinned objectui checkout, hotcrm (at the npm-published 17.4.0), duly and objectos; the type never appears in a PARAMETER position, so no seam accepts one; a missed in-repo constructor would fail `tsc`, and all four Type Check jobs were green. ⚠️ The residual is named, ⛔ not papered over: an npm consumer outside every reachable tree cannot be excluded by any sweep.

**Code byte-identity across the delta, verified three ways** (⛔ not taken on this seat's word): every `+`/`-` line in the `.ts` delta is a docblock line; a comment-stripped SHA-256 of `permission-set-projection.ts` is identical at both heads (`91679230362a21e4…`); and the other three files are `git diff --quiet` between the heads. ⇒ the judgments rendered on `7ea5f10a` carry over on **re-checked premises**, ⛔ not on assumption.

### ② Semver level

`minor`, and the changeset frontmatter agrees with the PR body's `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.

The constructor hazard does not reach `major`, on the repo's rules rather than the author's framing: `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `major` in the launch window outright and names the **BREAKING** banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition as the carriers of breaking-ness, 「not the level」 — so the question collapses to whether a banner is owed. The applied discriminator (`.changeset/s3-adapter-key-namespace.md:5-7`) grounds the banner in 「the accept set a consumer **writes against** narrows」; this is a **return** type with no input seam, so the set written against is unchanged and the set READ widens. Precedent on this very interface: 17.2.0 shipped required `unchanged` and `unreadable` as unbannered **Minor** (CHANGELOG `:2509-2519`).

⭐ The honest counter-reading is recorded rather than suppressed: the same gate's header says that **at GA** a required member on a published interface grades `major`, unqualified. On that reading the consequence is a banner plus an ADR-0087 marker — ⛔ **not** a different level. `minor` is right either way.

### ③ Boundary flags

**1 — Precision note, non-blocking, ⛔ not fixed here.** The new caveat names `SeedWriteRefusals` as the channel for an engine-rejected write. That holds on the boot loop, which passes a collector; the publish door passes none (`security-plugin.ts:3719`) and surfaces the same refusal as its own `applied === 0` → `success: false`. ⭐ The caveat's **operative** claim — 「increments no counter」 — is exact on **both** doors; only the channel clause is under-specified for one. The at-tier reviewer judged no fix required for this PR and this seat does not overrule that to buy a third prose round; it rides the next PR touching this prose, per 「搭下一个触碰它的 PR」.

**2 — A finding filed as its own card, ⛔ not a flag on this PR.** Pre-existing, outside the fence, unchanged by this diff: the publish door derives its failure reason by ELIMINATION and falls to 「publish carried no owning package」 for **every** zero-row outcome — including an engine-rejected write and an `unreadable` existence read, for which that text is **false**. ⚠️ The PR's own acceptance note calls that fallback 「correct」; it is correct for the **unowned** case only. Filed separately, with the reviewer's dedupe words.

**3 — Fence: inside.** The delta is two prose edits acting on ③.1/③.2 of the prior record and nothing else. Refusal, diagnostics, log line and tests untouched.

**4 — Existing assertions: none weakened or deleted.** The test file is byte-identical to `7ea5f10a`, `105/0` against base; no test in the repo does `toEqual`/`toStrictEqual` over a whole `PermissionSeedOutcome`.
